title: Petty cash of Mehak Stores
body: Mehak Stores keeps a petty cash book on the imprest system. On 1 June, the head cashier gives the petty cashier an imprest of Rs. 2,500. The petty cash book has analysis columns for Postage, Conveyance, Stationery and Miscellaneous. During June the petty cashier pays: postage stamps Rs. 310, auto and bus fares Rs. 460, pads and pencils Rs. 375, refreshments for staff Rs. 190 and cartage Rs. 85. Refreshments and cartage are entered in the Miscellaneous column because no separate column exists for them. On 30 June the columns are totalled, the balance is carried down, and on 1 July the head cashier reimburses the petty cashier. A petty cash account is kept in the ledger.

title: Analytical purchases book of Arora Traders, Delhi
body: Arora Traders of Delhi maintains an analytical purchases book with columns for Purchases, CGST, SGST and IGST. In August it makes two credit purchases of goods for resale. On 6 August it buys goods with a list price of Rs. 50,000 from Sethi and Sons, Delhi, less trade discount at 10%. On 20 August it buys goods with a list price of Rs. 40,000 from Malik Brothers, Haryana, less trade discount at 5%. GST at 18% applies to both purchases: on a purchase within the same state it is charged as CGST 9% and SGST 9%, and on a purchase from another state it is charged as IGST 18%. GST is calculated on the amount after trade discount, and each supplier's account is credited with the total amount of the invoice.
